featured_reviews.review_text: Yes this hotel is famous for Non veg food but if you are vegitarian planning to visit this hotel with your Non vegitarian friends then please don't even think of going here. First up of all they have nothing to offer for veg people. They dont even allow veg people to eat tiffin if you are carrying one. I visited this place with my officer friends out of which only i was vegitarian but i was carrying my tiffin but rude and arrogant staff didn't allow me to eat my vegitarian tiffin. All they had for veg people is poor quality veg thali. Plus the place is congested with no AC which make your dining experience very bad.

featured_reviews.name: Syamchand Nair
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you love seafood, this is the place to be! It is a casual, no-frills restaurant specializing in Konkan seafood cuisine.

​We visited for lunch around noon and were able to place our order without any wait. However, by 12:30 PM, the restaurant was almost full, so plan your visit early to avoid a queue.
​We ordered several Thalis: Prawns Masala, Prawns Curry, and Surmai Curry, along with a plate of Surmai Fry. The Prawns Masala was awesome, and the other thalis were good too. The Surmai Fry came with two good-sized pieces and was amazing. 😍

​The outdoor seating area needs a bit of maintenance, but otherwise, it was a great dining experience.

featured_reviews.name: Ravi kumar
featured_reviews.review_text: Great spicy food here. One of the risky items in non veg restaurants,  is getting fish food. We ordered pomfret fish fry meals. The fish was really fresh. Closest cuisine is Chettinad cuisine, so south Indians will feel at ease and appreciate the food even more.

featured_reviews.review_text: Decent place for a quick bite, not worth going out of your way for. Fish was overcooked and tough, definitely not fresh. Had the bombil fry, prawns fry, bangda and rawas curries. Overall lacked flavour- even the solkadi was very diluted and bland.

featured_reviews.name: Aakash Maji
featured_reviews.review_text:
In a very long time, I wasn’t filled with such a subtle and home-blend restaurant. Calling it a restaurant might be over exaggerating because this place is run by a family and the authentic Goan food that they serve just makes you feel at home. This charming place is nestled right beside the highway, amidst a small colony of homes. It’s seamlessly blended in, creating an atmosphere that feels more like a family’s home than a resting place.
We have got the Surmai Fish Curry Thali and the classic Chicken Masala Thali. Both were just amazing and homely to taste.

Their staffs are very friendly and sweet enough that you feel like home.

While the quantity of food didn’t quite match the pricing, the quality was great.

This is very good place to recommend for a family lunch/dinner. I am sure you won’t be disappointed with it. Enjoy.

I had a great dining experience at Ferry Wharf Seafood Restaurant – Bandra Reclamation (West) and really enjoyed every dish. 🦀🦞

featured_reviews.review_text:

featured_reviews.name: durgesh gawde
featured_reviews.review_text:
Jai Hind is a gem for seafood lovers, offering an impressive variety of dishes, generous portions, and prices that feel genuinely value-for-money. If you’re someone who appreciates fresh, well-cooked fish without burning a hole in your pocket, this restaurant easily stands out as one of the best options in the city.

One of the first things you notice at Jai Hind is the sheer range on the menu. From classics like Surmai Fry, Bombil Fry, Rawas Curry, and Prawns Koliwada to specials like Crab Masala and Tawa Pomfret, the restaurant ensures there’s something for every seafood enthusiast. What makes the experience even better is that the quality is consistent. The fish is fresh, perfectly marinated, and cooked with authentic coastal flavours that highlight Mumbai’s rich culinary heritage.

Quantity is another major plus. Unlike many seafood places where portions feel small for the price, Jai Hind gives you hearty servings that truly justify every rupee. Whether you order a thali or an à la carte dish, the plates come generously loaded, making it easy to share or enjoy as a filling meal on your own. Their fish thalis, in particular, are a standout—they offer a balanced combination of fried fish, curry, rice, chapati, and sides, making it both wholesome and satisfying.

The pricing is surprisingly reasonable, especially considering the rising cost of seafood in the city. For the quality and quantity provided, the restaurant manages to keep its rates fair, which is a big reason people return. It’s a great place for regular seafood cravings without feeling guilty about overspending.

The ambience is simple, clean, and comfortable—nothing overly fancy, but perfectly suited for a relaxed and enjoyable meal. Service is prompt, friendly, and attentive, with staff who are happy to recommend dishes based on your taste preferences.

featured_reviews.name: Nakul Janglay
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Fresh Catch by Francis recently after hearing a lot about it and honestly came back with mixed feelings.

We tried -

Mushroom Butter Garlic was decent, nothing wrong with it, but nothing memorable either.

Bombil Rava Fry was probably the better dish of the lot. Crispy, tasty, and enjoyable.

Bangda Ambotic Curry was good, but felt like a standard Goan curry. Not something I’d go back specifically for.

Crab Meat Spicy Masala.
It was more like a regular seafood bhurji than a standout crab dish. Now where close to justifying the exorbitant price being charged.

Pomfret Hara Bhara Tawa Fry.
The biggest letdown. The fish didn’t feel particularly fresh, the taste was quite average, and the pricing for a small medium sized portion felt just too steep. For that kind of money (or even less) you can easily get a proper wholesome seafood thali elsewhere.

Overall, the food wasn’t bad, just pretty underwhelming for the pricing and hype. Maybe Goan flavors are intentionally subtler and my palate leans more towards Konkani/Malvani seafood.

If I’m spending that kind of money on seafood in Mumbai, places like Nav Chaitanya and Gajalee still set the benchmark for me in terms of flavor, consistency and value.

featured_reviews.review_text: I visited Fresh Catch on 4 June 2026 and it was excellent!  I asked the bartender to create me a great custom drink and he exceeded my expectations with refreshing and unique creations. My waiter, Lawrence, was extremely helpful in bombil suggestions as well as sourcing from off menu fish. Try Fresh Catch you won’t be disappointed with the drinks, food or service. Ask for Lawrence!

featured_reviews.name: Siddharth Bose
featured_reviews.review_text:
I got to know about this place through YouTube channel Curly Tales, that discusses the favourite food of various celebrities around the country. This place was heavily recommended over the channel by Indian cricket legend Sachin Tendulkar, hence making it easier in terms of choosing the place.

It's a restaurant that serves a vast array of seafood items and some standout dishes that are worthy of being called Legendary.

The dishes I ordered during my visit were Bomblivi fish fry, Prawn Rechada and a bowl of Mixed Sea food pulao.
Add to that, 2 mugs of kingfisher beer to help in aiding the food down the stomach correctly.

The outcome, i was absolutely in wonderland after gorging on their food like there was no tomorrow.

The Prawn Rechada was simply outstanding to another level. The flavours, reminding me of the coastal beaches of India really gave an everlasting taste to hook onto.

The mixed seafood pulao was again another real dish that was crafted amazingly by their chefs. The homemade spice aromas were so imminent that it wasn't a surprise about finishing up the dish by myself.

Overall service and management deserves a 5/5. Food deserves a 5/5 as well .

Keep up the good work.

We ordered for a chicken thali, a pomfret thali and an surmai thali and a tisrya sukkah.
Was totally disappointed when the food came, the tisrya sukkha seemed like tisrya masala and was very sweet. The surmai thali was not upto the mark, surmai was very small, I have never had such small piece of surmai in any of the fish outlet.

I will not recommend this restaurant to anyone, specially who is a fish lover.

featured_reviews.name: Pereira Gynel
featured_reviews.review_text:
This place has such an amazing tropical ambience. You are welcomed by soulful Goan music, and the vibe is relaxed and unhurried. The servers don’t rush you, making it a perfect spot to truly enjoy your meal.

Mr. Merwin, the manager, took great care of us, and our servers Sonia and Edwin were humble, polite, and very prompt, obliging us with every request.

The food is unlike anything you’ve tasted.. authentic Goan cuisine rooted deeply in the culture and spices of Goa. Every dish is beautifully presented, with thoughtful plating that elevates the experience without being overdone. The cutlery, plates, and glassware are aesthetically pleasing and enhance the dining experience, without robbing you of quantity. Portions are generous and satisfying.

From the big plates, we had the Traditional Pork Sorpatel with rice, Goan-style chilli chicken, and Surmai fish curry rice. The sorpatel was so authentic it made my mum emotional...it brought back memories of old friends who had cooked traditional pork dishes in her younger days. The Goan-style chilli chicken was the standout dish of the afternoon...smooth, succulent, and packed with a powerful flavour punch. The surmai fish curry rice felt like something an old granny had made, warm, comforting, and soulful.

From the small plates, we tried the Goan fried chicken with spicy mayo...six generous boneless strips, made to order, pairing perfectly with lime and the spicy mayo. The grilled squid stuffed with crab was outstanding, with the masala truly stealing the show. The prawn balchao masala stuffed forminhas crispy tarts were tangy and well-made; while not my personal favourite, they were only overshadowed by stronger dishes. The tender coconut and raw mango salad was light, tropical, refreshing, and beautifully balanced.

For drinks, we had the Coconut Boy Refresher, Kokum Spritz, and Tamarind Trails. These are not your usual cocktails... Goan spices and flavours take centre stage, and an open mind is needed to fully enjoy them.

Coconut Boy truly lives up to its promise of 'fresh' and delivers an experience that transports you straight to Goa. Highly recommended even if you’re simply looking for some relaxed downtime with exceptional food and service.

featured_reviews.name: Everything On A Plate EOAP
featured_reviews.review_text:
AMBIENCE:

Despite being located at a busy intersection, the instant you come inside, you are taken to a tranquil and unexpectedly quiet environment. Amidst the dim lights and décor paying ode to the Goan theme, what we appreciated the most was the ample open space to move around and even dance (which our daughter did multiple times throughout the night).

FOOD:
Vegetable Cheese Rissois: Though the classic Portuguese fried pastry is usually filled with meat, we tried the vegetarian version and were not disappointed. It starts with a crumbly-soft bite which leads to a minced vegetables mixed with cheese that definitely melts in your mouth.

Mapusa Market toast with Cheese & Green Chilli: Coconut boys take on the chilli cheese toast with a twist. On first look it’s just your average cheese chilli toast, but one bite into it and you hit a tangy punch which took us by surprise…. It was mango aachaar! ‘Who would’ave thunk?’ This dish did have some mixed opinions!

Choris Chilli Fry: Choriz tossed with chilli, onion, tomato teamed up with warm, fluffy poee… we absolutely left licking our fingers. Would have gone for round two but there was more to be relished on the menu.

Grilled Squid Stuffed with Crab: A host suggestion that we absolutely jumped at the mention of! Crab meat tossed in Recheado, stuffed into a squid & grilled… a lot of effort goes into this. Hints of spice married with the sweetness of the crab meat and the bite of squid… a messy meal you must try at least once! Definitely big brownie points for the squid NOT being chewy.

Mushroom & vegetables slow cooked with Xacuti masala: A medley of steamed veggies (Mushroom, carrot, potato, cauliflower) tossed in a Xacuti gravy. You have an option of Poee or steamed rice to accompany it and we went with the latter. We requested them to hold back the spice a bit for our toddler & it’s wholesome, earthy, slightly-sweet coconut-ty broth was welcomed with a smack of the lips.

Serradura: This simple pudding can go awry in so many ways… And believe me, we've tasted some absolute disasters. But coconut boy absolutely nailed-it! The crumbly, biscuit dust alternated with fluffy, light whipped cream was what we devoured at the end of a great meal. Not too sweet, not too dense… just perfect.

Service: The service undoubtedly elevated our entire experience! We had Siddhesh giving us amazing recommendations and making sure we had everything we needed. Akbar stopped by with some fantastic banter, and last but not least, Faustin, whom our daughter adored and sat with virtually the entire dinner, allowing us to savour every bite!

SUMMING UP: If you love Goan food, it’s definitely an experience you do not want to miss. Right from the décor to the service, it’s comfy, cozy and warm. The cost is a bit on the higher end but the quality and flavors are worth every penny.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Jai Hind Lunch Home,  Pali Naka,  Bandra (west)

Jai Hind is a brightest shining star of the galaxy of coastal cuisine restaurants in Mumbai.  With the few branches spread across the city,  this branch at Bandra,  Pali Naka is their first branch.  The other one is on the Linking Road, which seems to be rather spacious and well furnished.  But as a foodie, my hunt is always for a 'Value for money'  restaurants with excellent quality and quantity and this desire of mime gets fulfilled only in humble homely restaurants.  This branch at Pali Naka has been renovated recently and has only five tables in all.  I recommend to reserve a table in the evening as its a very old and famous restaurant in the area and gets filled quite soon.

The list of dishes we ordered :

1.  Patra Ni Macchi (Basa)
2. Bombil Thali
3. Chicken Sukka Thali

Let me begin with the most yummiest first. The chicken sukka was simply top quality stuff made with supreme perfection. It was creamy with great blend of masalas and literally made us lick our fingers till the end.  The chicken pieces were one of the softest and well marinated ones I ever had.  The Bombil was crispy and crunchy on the outside and soft juicy within. The soul kadi (pink broth)  was thick and made with actual coconut milk.  The texture of the chapatis were homely and rice was soft, fresh and well cooked.

Patra Ni Macchi was steamed to ultimate perfection,  which retained the original flavour of the soft melting Basa fish.  The green stuffing on it was blend of spicy and sour.

Over all,  A must visit restaurant..
Staff is helpful

I feel like it's a good place, all the place needs is a good crowd and a motivated, confident staff, rest all things are great including ambience, music, seating etc.

description:

featured_reviews.name: vidisha pisal
featured_reviews.review_text:
The restaurant covers India’s west + southwest coast, plus Kerala. All of them are big on seafood, coconut, and bold spices but each has its own vibe

- *Mangalorean*: Known for fiery, coconut-heavy curries and _ghee roast_. Uses Byadagi chilies for color + flavor. Lots of pork, seafood, and kori roti.
- *Malvani*: From Maharashtra’s Konkan belt. Dry coconut, kokum, and tirphal/sichuan pepper give it a tangy, peppery kick. Famous for fish curries and thalis.
- *Konkan/Goan*: Coconut + kokum again, but Goan food also has Portuguese influence — vindaloo, cafreal, and lots of vinegar. Seafood + pork are staples.
- *Kerala*: Coconut oil, curry leaves, black pepper, and rice-based sides like appam and puttu. Big on fish, beef, and subtle but complex spice.

*The Ambience & Service*
- *Ambience*: When a place calls itself “one of the finest” with coastal food, expect warm lighting, usually means clean, spacious, not too loud.
- *Staff*: “Very generous” usually means attentive service, good portion sizes, and staff who’ll guide you through the menu if you’re new to coastal food.

### *The Food — Dish by Dish*

*Starters / Tandoor*
- *Tandoor Soya Chaap*: Soya chunks marinated in curd, ginger-garlic, and tandoori masala, then charred in the tandoor. Smoky, juicy, with that red tandoori exterior. Great veg option that mimics kebabs.
- *Prawns Ghee Roast*: A Mangalorean classic. Prawns tossed in a thick, caramelized masala of ghee, Byadagi + red chilies, garlic, and curry leaves.

*Mains / Thalis*
- *Surmai Thali*: _Surmai_ = Kingfish/Seer fish. A thali means a full plate: fried or curry surmai as the hero, plus rice/bhakri, solkadi, a veg side, pickle, and sometimes a prawns or clams sukka. Coastal thalis are all about balance — spicy fish, cooling solkadi, and rice.
- *Mutton Thali*:Kolhapuri style mutton. Dark, spicy curry with dagad phool and dry coconut, fall-off-bone meat. Comes with bhakri or vade, rice, and sides. Hearty and peppery.
- *Kori Roti with Curry*: Mangalorean comfort food. _Kori_ = chicken curry with a thin, red, coconut-based gravy. _Roti_ = not wheat roti but crisp, dry rice wafers that you crush and soak in the curry. It goes from crunchy to soft in seconds.
- *Neer Dosa*: From coastal Karnataka. _Neer_ = water. Paper-thin, soft, lacy dosa made from just rice batter. No fermentation, so it’s mild and perfect for mopping up spicy ghee roast or chicken curry.
- *Appam*: Kerala’s bowl-shaped rice + coconut pancake. Crispy lacy edges, soft spongy center. Made for sopping up stew or curry.
- *Surmai Garlic Tawa Fry*: Thick surmai steak marinated in chili-garlic paste, rava or rice flour coating, then shallow-fried on a tawa. Spicy, garlicky, crusty outside and flaky inside.

*Mocktails*
- *Green Valley Mocktail
- *Lovely Smile Mocktail
*Dessert*
- *Gadbad*: Mangalore’s iconic ice cream sundae. Translates to “hurry-scurry”. Served in a tall glass with layers of 3-4 ice cream flavors, jelly, fresh fruit, dry fruits, and nuts. Chaotic, colorful, and meant to be mixed as you eat.

basically did a coastal crawl in one meal — tandoor for smoky start, ghee roast + tawa fry for spice, thalis for the full experience, and neer dosa/appam/kori roti to try all the classic carb pairings. Then cooled it down with mocktails and ended with Mangalore’s most famous dessert.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Last evening, visited O Pedro at Godrej BKC to catch up with friends, and overall it turned out to be a lively and enjoyable experience. The restaurant definitely has a strong personality of its own — vibrant ambience, energetic crowd, good music, and a stylish Goan-Latin inspired vibe that makes it feel different from the usual BKC dining places.

The ambience and overall vibe are honestly one of the biggest strengths of O Pedro. The place feels warm, colourful, and social without becoming too loud or chaotic. It’s ideal for group outings and long conversations over food and drinks. The interiors are beautifully done, and the energy of the place keeps the atmosphere upbeat throughout the evening.

Coming to the food and drinks, we ordered quite a variety.

The Stranger & Sons cocktail was refreshing and smooth with balanced botanical flavours. It paired really well with the starters.

The Crab Ros Omelette was flavourful and rich, with soft eggs wrapped around well-seasoned crab filling. It had a comforting yet indulgent taste.

The Malaki Indian Tonic was light, crisp, and refreshing, making it a good accompaniment during the meal.

The Guava Pineapple Sour had a tropical sweetness balanced nicely with a sour finish. Refreshing and enjoyable without being overly sweet.

The Choriz Chilly Fry (Gluten Free) was one of the highlights. Packed with bold Goan flavours, smoky spice, and excellent texture, it paired wonderfully with drinks.

The Grilled Chicken Peri Peri was juicy and well-marinated with balanced heat levels. The chicken was cooked properly without drying out.

The Picante Highballin cocktail had a nice spicy-citrus profile and worked very well for those who enjoy slightly stronger flavours.

The All Poee Basket and freshly served Poee were excellent accompaniments. Soft, fresh, and authentic, they complemented the spicy dishes beautifully.

The Cardoz’s Chicken Chilli Fry had strong coastal flavours with a nice spice kick. The preparation felt rustic and flavourful.

The Monkey Shoulder (60ml) was smooth and enjoyable as expected for whisky lovers.

The Roasted Lamb Chops were tender, juicy, and cooked well. The seasoning was balanced and allowed the flavour of the meat to stand out nicely.

We ended with Aunty Li’s Serradura, which was creamy, light, and a perfect dessert to finish the meal without feeling too heavy.

The staff throughout the evening was courteous, attentive, and helpful. Service was fairly smooth despite the restaurant being busy.

However, there were a few things that slightly impacted the overall experience.

The first was the extremely high cover charge for confirmed bookings. Charging ₹1,000 per person through food apps for securing a preferred time slot felt excessive, even though the amount gets adjusted in the final bill. featured_reviews.review_text:
While Juhu is famous for its beach snacks and high-end cafes, the real magic happens in the kitchens that treat seafood with the respect it deserves. This isn't just a meal; it’s a deep dive into the culinary traditions of the Konkan coast.
The Ambiance
Don't expect minimalist chic. The vibe here is "busy Sunday lunch." It’s loud, efficient, and smells heavenly. The decor is usually simple because the owners know you aren't there to look at the walls—you’re there for the crab.
The Standout Dishes
Bombil Fry (Bombay Duck): A local must-have. It’s light, crisp on the outside, and melts like butter the moment it hits your tongue. If it doesn't crunch, it's not authentic.
Butter Garlic Pepper Crab: This is the messiest, most rewarding dish on the menu. The meat is succulent, and the sauce is so rich you’ll want to mop it up with a Neer Dosa.
Surmai (Kingfish) Thali: For the solo diner or the traditionalist. A thick, spicy masala fry served alongside a bowl of soul-warming Sol Kadhi (a pink, tangy coconut milk appetizer).
The Verdict
The service is brisk—they expect you to eat, enjoy, and make room for the next hungry patron. It’s a bit pricey compared to street food, but for the freshness of the catch, it’s worth every rupee.
Pro Tip: Always ask for the "Catch of the Day" before looking at the menu. If the Pomfret is fresh, don't overthink it—just order it.

customer_updates.text: If there’s a brand that embodies the safari gold standard, it’s Singita, which runs 19 lodges and camps across South Africa, Zimbabwe, Tanzania and Rwanda. Ebony Lodge, overlooking the Sand River in a private concession in the leopard-rich Sabi Sands Game Reserve, was the one that started it all, back in 1993. But in some ways Singita’s other lodges (we adore the nature-modernist Sweni lodge) had overtaken its traditional aesthetic—until a richly textured redesign led by Cape Town designers Cécile and Boyd was unveiled in spring 2024. The new Ebony Lodge—with the indoor-outdoor stepped central area that descends toward the river, and the glass and canvas that has replaced walls in the 12 richly textured suites—is more flowing, more immersed in nature. Singita’s game drives are always next-level, and for us, private sightings, like of a tree-bound leopard chillingly devouring an impala, were followed by blissful moments by our private plunge pool watching elephants loll in the riverbed. The new Ebony is smarter than ever but, happily, remains a classic.

featured_reviews.name: Janhavi Raut
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Goankar Cuisine in Mumbai, and overall it turned out to be a mixed but interesting dining experience. When we first arrived, the restaurant was completely empty, but as we started ordering, the place quickly became busy and was soon filled with many guests.

We began with crab Manchow soup, but honestly it tasted more like a regular Manchow soup as the crab quantity was very minimal and there wasn’t much seafood flavour in it. After that, we tried prawns lollipop, which unfortunately was not good. The texture felt sticky and unusual, and it was difficult to even recognize the prawns properly, so we didn’t enjoy that dish.

However, the experience improved with the next dishes. The squid Koliwada was excellent — very crunchy and perfectly cooked. It was definitely one of the better starters we tried.

The staff member Mr. Akash, who was serving us, was very helpful and gave good suggestions. On his recommendation, we tried chicken Kalakari, which turned out to be really tasty. It had a rich, authentic Indian-style chicken masala and was well marinated with great flavour.

For the main course, he first suggested chicken vindaloo, but since it is slightly tangy, we decided not to order it. Instead, he recommended chicken Xacuti (Shakoti), which was excellent and full of authentic Goan flavours. Along with that, we tried prawns masala dry, which was honestly amazing and one of the highlights of the meal.

We paired the dishes with Amboli, Ghavna, and rice bhakri. The rice bhakri was very large and quite filling, making it a great accompaniment to the curries.

For dessert, we tried Ukdiche Modak ice cream, which was truly a game changer. It was such a unique dessert that we ended up ordering another one because everyone at the table loved it. It was a really creative and delicious twist on the traditional modak.

Overall, despite a few disappointing starters, the main course, dessert, and the helpful service by Mr. Akash made the experience really enjoyable. If you visit, definitely try the squid Koliwada, prawns masala dry, chicken Xacuti, and the Ukdiche Modak ice cream.

featured_reviews.name: Vinayak Moorthy
featured_reviews.review_text:
Goaikar – where the fish is larger than life and the flavours come with a warning ⚠️🐟

Walked into Goaikar with big Goan expectations and walked out with an even bigger respect for their humongous fish portions. Let’s start with the clear winners of the day — the prawns lollipop and the stuffed bombil fry. Absolute show-stealers. Crisp, juicy, perfectly seasoned… the kind of dishes that make you nod silently while chewing because words fail you.

Next up, the iconic Goan ros omelette with poee — decent, comforting, but didn’t quite give us that nostalgic roadside Goan punch. More “okay okay” than “arre waah”.

Now to the grand thali saga 🍽️
We ordered the Surmai fish thali, Pomfret special thali, and Bombil thali — and oh my God, the fishes were MONSTERS. Fried to golden perfection, fresh, meaty, and clearly not shy about their presence on the plate. Total paisa-vasool when it comes to the fish itself.

But (there’s always a but)… the accompanying curries and gravies came in hot — and not the fun kind 🌶️🔥
For us, especially with a Goan mom in the house, the gravies felt too spicy and a little off-track from traditional Goan flavours. More fire, less finesse. Authentic Goa whispered… while chilli shouted.

Just when our taste buds were waving a white flag, dessert arrived like a saviour from heaven — Ukdiche Modak Ice Cream 🍨✨
Sweet, comforting, innovative, and honestly the icing on the cake (or modak on the ice cream?). A perfect, soulful ending that brought smiles back instantly.

From a value standpoint, pricing sits firmly at the premium end, with most dishes priced at ₹500 and above. While the generous seafood portions partially justify this, the ukdiche modak ice cream, though innovative and flavourful, was served in a modest portion at ₹180, feeling more like a tasting than a finale.

It is also worth noting that several social media claims suggesting a 10% discount at the restaurant did not reflect our experience, and no such concession was available during our visit—something diners may wish to verify in advance.

What truly elevated the experience was the service. Our order taker, Aditya, was exceptionally warm, attentive, and knowledgeable, guiding us with genuine enthusiasm. The entire service team mirrored this standard—courteous, efficient, and consistently welcoming—adding a layer of hospitality that made the meal feel relaxed and well cared for.

Final verdict:
Goaikar nails seafood portions and frying like a boss, experiments boldly with flavours, and redeems everything with dessert magic. A must-visit for fish lovers — just keep a glass of water (and an open mind for spice) handy 😄🔥🐠

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (minus half a star for the chilli ambush)

A jewel worth your moolah! Nestled in the by-lanes of Borivali, this little gem is a sparkler, for sure. Your search for authentic Malvani cuisine ends here.
Be it the use of spices, the freshness of the ingredients, the quantity, the quality and the authenticity...all scream 'Fantastic'!

The fish is fresh. The solkadi is yummy. The JOWARI BHAKRI is super soft..😋
The Kothimbir wadis are delightful too.
The fish gravy is a tad spicy...not for the faint-hearted. But just the way Malvani cuisine should be.
The fresh lime soda is decent.
The absolute highlight: The modaks, though it was a 20 minute wait.  Fresh. Authentic. Mouth-watering, to say the least. And the drizzle of ghee over the modaks...👌😋😋...oohhlaalaa..next level. A++

Definitely worth a return...over and over. If consistency prevails.
Thumbs up!! 👍👌

featured_reviews.review_text:
Ambiance: Simple, soothing, with both indoor and outdoor sitting. Located at Babhai Naka, Borivali.

Our experience: We went in for dinner on a weekday. The place was largely empty and quiet. Took them 20 mins to take our first order despite having only 4 tables being served including ours.

We ordered the following dishes:
• Bombil Fry: The coating was way too thicker and the bombil hardly present. Could barely taste the bombil.
• Prawn koliwada: Again the coating overpowered the flavor of prawns.
• Bangda Thali and Ravas thali: Both thalis were exactly the same with the same fish curry, a tiny serving of prawn preparation, another tiny serving of matki usal in one thali and another random gravy in the bangda thalis. We weren't asked about our preferences for wada, chapati or bhakri. So one thali came with wadas, the other with chapati and on placing the order the third, we were asked about our preference for chapati or bhakri then informed bhakri is probabaly over. So we okayed chapati but were served wadas.

We also ordered another plate of extra chapati which they didnt have and offered wadas but none reached our table even after 2 reminders.

Finally we finished our meals and then asked for the bill which had the extra cost of wadas which we ordered and never recieved and also for the wada in thali which we weren't informed were charged extra but were given as they didnt have chapatis or bhakris.

They did change the bill on being informed.

We also asked for regular water which we recieved almost at the end of the meal after being reminded for the fifth time.

Service: Slow, and confused even when there were just 2-3 tables with people only.

While we understand it was end if the day and hence the food there was over and also probably that is why there were many errors & delays in service. But the overall experience and food were not upto the mark or hype.

featured_reviews.name: Chef Vaidehi Pathare
featured_reviews.review_text:
This was my second visit to Pangat in Nancy Colony, Borivali. I had a good experience earlier, so I came again on a rainy Friday evening with my family. It took us a good 15 minutes to get a table. The restaurant has both indoor and outdoor seating. This time we chose to sit inside. The place looks classy with minimalistic decor, and I liked the overall ambience.

We started with Veg Manchow Soup, Chicken Kalimiri Kebab, and Crab Lollipop. The soup was perfect for the weather and tasted really good. The Chicken Kalimiri Kebab tasted good and was cooked well, but I found a thread in the last piece, which was really disappointing. The staff took it to the kitchen when we showed it, but there was no response after that from their end. The Crab Lollipop tasted like it was frozen and not freshly made in their kitchen. Definitely not something I would order again.

For the main course, we ordered Veg Thali, Chicken Hyderabadi, Jeera Rice, Chapati, and Rice Bhakri. The thali was nice and filling. The Chicken Hyderabadi had good flavours but I personally felt it could have been a bit spicier. It had more of spinach-like aftertaste. The Rice Bhakri was soft and fresh, which I really liked. The Chapati was good and the Jeera Rice was simple and comforting.

The food overall was decent, but the service needs a lot of improvement. We had to call the staff multiple times just to get water or basic things. Many times, they completely ignored us, which was disappointing. When I raised this with the manager, he just listened and didn’t say anything. I honestly feel service matters as much as the food, and that part really fell short during our visit. I have had a better experience here before, so I do hope they take this feedback positively.

Ratings:
Quality - 3/5
Quantity - 4/5
Service - 3/5
Price - ₹2100 for 4 people

featured_reviews.name: Naresh Shirodkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Pangat is one of those places you walk into with high expectations, especially given its reputation for Malvani thalis and coastal favourites. Having been regular patrons for many years, this place has held a certain nostalgic charm for us, which made our recent visits all the more noticeable in contrast.
We sampled a fairly elaborate spread, including their Bombil Thali, Surmai Thali, Prawns Thali, Mandeli fry, along with add ons like the much talked about Crab Lollypop, Bheja Masala, Kalva Sukka, Chicken Potli Kebab, and also revisited dishes we have enjoyed in the past like the keema pattice, bombil fry, and mutton masala.
While the menu continues to promise a seafood lover’s delight, the overall experience, unfortunately, felt average this time around. The Bombil and Surmai fry had the expected crispness, but lacked that depth of flavour and freshness that truly elevates coastal cuisine. The curries across thalis felt somewhat one dimensional, missing the robust, layered Malvani masala profile one associates with Pangat. Even the basics like chapatis and bhakris, which form the backbone of such meals, could be softer, fresher, and more refined.
On a more specific note, the tisrya masala (dry) felt quite chewy, almost rubbery in texture, taking away from what is otherwise a delightful dish when done right. The solkadhi, too, seemed to miss that refreshing kokam forward tang we have experienced here earlier and elsewhere.
That said, what truly stood out and deserves full credit was the service and hospitality. The staff handled everything with genuine warmth, attentiveness, and honesty. From guiding through the menu to ensuring timely service, their effort and intent were clearly heartfelt, and it did make a meaningful difference to the overall dining experience.
Pangat certainly has the foundation of a great dining destination, and perhaps it is just a matter of revisiting the fundamentals. With a bit more attention to core elements like breads, curries, and flavour balance, it has every potential to regain the consistency and charm it was once known for.
For now, a place that still offers variety, but one we hope will soon rediscover the flavours that made it special for us over the years.

featured_reviews.name: Ujwal Dawrung
featured_reviews.review_text:
The food at this restaurant was actually good, especially the prawns, but the service was extremely disappointing. The waiters were very slow and careless while taking orders. We ordered prawns, but instead they served us someone else’s used chutney, which was completely unacceptable and unhygienic.

The hospitality was the worst part of the experience. The staff behavior was not polite, and the waiters lacked basic professionalism and courtesy. Good food alone is not enough when the service and customer handling are this poor. Very disappointing experience overall.

featured_reviews.name: Sagar Jadhav
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited this hotel/restaurant, but unfortunately, the experience was not good.

The biggest issue was the service — it was extremely slow. After placing the order, the food took a very long time to arrive, which made the waiting time frustrating.

Secondly, the taste of the food was disappointing. Some of the dishes were excessively salty, which completely ruined the overall experience.

The ambience was decent, but there is a serious need to improve both service speed and food quality.
I hope the management takes this feedback seriously and makes improvements.
